title: Speaker Forsthoffer Bars Mi Hazánk Leader Toroczkai From Parliament Sessions Over Slur Against Magyar
detail: Speaker of the National Assembly Ágnes Forsthoffer excluded Mi Hazánk faction leader László Toroczkai from this week's parliamentary sessions on the evening of September 8, after Toroczkai called PM Péter Magyar a 'disgusting worm' during a personal statement defending his party against corruption allegations. Forsthoffer ruled the remark violated the constitutionally protected right to human dignity, stating she 'firmly rejects all statements that seriously violate human dignity against anyone.' Toroczkai retains the right to vote but is barred from other floor proceedings for the week. The episode is the first high-profile use of Forsthoffer's disciplinary powers as Speaker against a sitting far-right MP since she took the chair in May.

title: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats — First Such Move Since 2018
detail: Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced on September 8 that Hungary declared 10 Russian diplomatic staff persona non grata for engaging in activities 'unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention,' without disclosing specifics. It is Hungary's first public expulsion of Russian diplomats since 2018 and the first since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 — a period in which Orbán's government expelled none while most EU states expelled dozens. Budapest said the move does not sever diplomatic relations and that necessary dialogue with Moscow will continue. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called it an 'extremely unfriendly step' driven by a 'Russophobic lobby in Budapest' and promised a response that would be 'harsh and painful.' The expulsion follows Hungary's June pledge to back a full year-long extension of EU sanctions on Russia, reinforcing Magyar's realignment away from Orbán's Moscow-friendly posture.

media.caption: Hungary expels 10 Russian diplomats, ending eight years without a public expulsion
